title: [Decision] Approval shape for bulk re-key — two approvers for a batch, one for a single-org rotation
description:
## BLUF

@peter's proposal: a **batch** re-key needs two approvers; a **single-org** rotation needs one. The shape needs deciding, but it **cannot be implemented until** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) **lands** — the shared platform-admin account cannot make a two-approver rule real, because the same credential can satisfy both approvals.

Carried over from @peter's own candidate list on KS-480, unchanged.

## Detail

Open questions for the decision:

* Who counts as an approver, and is the *requester* allowed to be one of the two?
* Is approval synchronous (the call blocks) or a request/approve/execute flow with a record between the steps?
* What is the break-glass path when a genuine incident cannot wait for a second approver, and what does it cost in audit terms?
* Does the second approval cover the whole batch, or the specific list of refs (so the list cannot be edited after approval)?

**Blocked on:** [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities).

**Done when:** the shape is agreed and recorded here, with the break-glass path named explicitly rather than left implicit.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

nodes.body: Re-filed as its own issue now the cap has cleared: **[PS-740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-740/sk-key-recovery-a-keyinvalid-state-a-supported-inlet-for-a-rotated)** — the S-side half of the grant-driven re-key (KeyInvalid state, rotated-key inlet, grant drain, expiry visibility). Linked Related from here.

## Proposal from the S side: make the re-key **grant-driven**, with S as the executor

Context: investigating key expiry/recovery after S's local provisioning key lapsed on 2026-08-31 (PS-319). Verified in code on both sides, S today has **no recovery path at all** — re-registration returns no key (§4), `rotate: true` is 403'd for a provisioning-key caller by Guardrail 1 (`platform.ts:503`), and even an admin-run rotation dead-ends because S has no inlet to receive the key (`EncryptedApiKey` is written only by the registrar's first mint). The full S-side write-up is on PS-319 (pending re-file as its own ticket — the workspace issue cap is hit).

**The shape.** Keep Guardrail 1's human-in-the-loop, but change *who executes*:

1. A platform admin mints a **re-key grant** — one-time, time-boxed (hours), naming an explicit list of `externalRef`s (or all-for-tenant), recorded as its own audited object.
2. `register-connector` accepts `rotate: true` from a **provisioning-scoped** caller **only when accompanied by a live grant** covering that `externalRef`; the grant is consumed per ref. Revoke-on-rotate (KS-577) folded in.
3. S's registration sweep, given the grant via its secret store, drains every dead-key row itself and stores the returned keys exactly as first registration does.

**Why this over the admin-executed bulk endpoint as currently scoped:** with the admin executing, N plaintext keys come back to a human who then has to get them into S — a path S does not even have today, and one that puts operational secrets through hands and clipboards. With S executing under a grant, plaintext never leaves the two systems, the *same* mechanism recovers a **greenfield S against a populated K** (the `AlreadyRegistered`-no-key terminal case from S's DR facts), and the grant *is* the approval artifact KS-582 is asking for.

**It answers KS-582's open questions directly:** approver = whoever mints the grant (two-approver batch = a grant needing two mints/co-signs once KS-579 gives per-person admins; one for a single-ref grant); the flow is request → approve (grant minted) → execute (S drains), with the grant as the record between steps; the ref list is fixed at mint, so it cannot be edited after approval; break-glass is the existing S-side `UseConnectorKeyAuth=false` fallback, already alarmed three ways, so no new break-glass path is needed here.

**Input for Stuart's KS-577 cutover question** (his decision, not mine): when S is the executor, the cutover window collapses — S holds the new key the instant the response lands and the old one is revoked in the same operation; anything in flight in that sub-second gap 401s once and is retried by the refresher, which already handles exactly that. No grace window needed.

**Companion ask, small and independent:** a `whoami`-style read returning the *calling* key's id/scopes/`expiresAt`. Nothing today lets a key learn when it expires, so S cannot warn ahead — the 08-31 lapse was invisible until it bit.
